catalog_quote: 2.4. Contrastive Stress. Contrastive stress is seen in the following examples: cika 'he chips', cakd 'he vomits', boca-t 'a fish (species)', bocdr 'a turtle', pdsa 'he arrived (going upriver away from speaker)', pasd 'salt lick'. ... 8.1. Primary Word Stress. Although primary word stress is not predictable in Guayabero — the syllable bearing primary word stress can occur word initially, medially, or finally with no cooccurrence restrictions — it always occurs on either the ultimate or penultimate syllable of the grammatical stem, thereby identifying the stem in speech. Furthermore, syllable-final consonant clusters occur only in stem-final syllables bearing primary stress, so the maximum expansion of a syllable is always associated with primary stress. (2) Deciding source: a 31-pp SIL phonology article (1985) with an explicit suprasegmentals section, minimal pairs, and a rhythm-group analysis; its Spanish original (Keels 1984, downloaded now, scanned of printed p.125) says the same ('no es predecible.. ultima o penultima silaba de la raiz gramatical'). Glottolog 5.1 lists no reference grammar, dissertation, or instrumental study for Guayabero; the 2012 pedagogical grammar (held) and the 2022 dictionary (downloaded now) give no placement rule, though the dictionary's accent-marked headwords vary in stress position as expected under lexical stress. sources.quote: 'A pesar de que el acento primario de palabra no es predecible en guayabero -- la silaba que posee acento primario puede ocurrir al comienzo de la palabra, en el medio de esta, o al final, y no hay restricciones co-ocurrentes -- siempre se presenta, o bien en la ultima silaba, o en la penultima de la raiz gramatical, identificando en esta forma la raiz.' (Spanish original says 'raiz' = root where the 1985 English says 'grammatical stem'.)

sources.quote: No rule for stress placement is stated. The orthography section only notes that diphthongs 'por lo general se acentuan en la primera vocal' and that ph/th are aspirated 'en posicion inicial de una silaba acentuada'; headwords carry a written acute accent whose position varies lexically (buya 'flecha', jela vs. athi 'sainos', jalwek 'buscar', kaka 'oso perezoso', to'a 'mandar'), consistent with unpredictable stress within a final two-syllable window but not an explicit statement.
